source.notes: Official CISCE specimen paper with answer key in one PDF. Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2026' (question paper, PDF pages 1-11) or 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2026' (answer key, PDF pages 12-27); examYear=2026 is the examination year the specimen is published for. It is a SPECIMEN, not a past board paper. No paper/set/series code is printed (the subject code appears only in the file name), so those fields are null. Official answers are taken only from the answer key in the same PDF, trimmed to value points. Cognitive-level tags are recorded as printed. 'page' is the physical PDF page of the question text. Question paper: 20 questions, Sections A (20 x 1 mark), B (7 x 2), C (7 x 3), D (5 x 5), maximum 80. Internal choice ('OR') is printed in Questions 5, 6, 7 (B), 13, 14, 15 (C) and 16, 17, 18 (D); each alternative is a separate entry sharing a choiceGroup. Question 1 (i)-(xx) are separate 1-mark entries. Multi-part questions whose parts share one stem (9, 14(i), 15(ii), 16(ii), 17(ii), 18) are kept together with printed part marks in the text. Math-italic glyphs in the text layer are written as plain letters; powers, fractions and subscripts were rebuilt from the page renders (flagged MEDIUM). The answer key itself has two internal inconsistencies (Q1(v), Q1(xv): printed option letter disagrees with its own stated answer); correctOption is omitted there.

The Cartesian product A × A has 16 elements among which are (0,2) and (1,3). Which of the following statements is correct?
Statement I: It is possible to determine the set A.
Statement II: A × A contains the element (3,2).
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statements I is false and Statement II is true.
extractionIssues: Official answer key is internally inconsistent: it prints option letter (c) but its text ('Both I and II', 'Both statements are true') matches option (a). correctOption omitted; editor to resolve.

officialAnswer.text: (c) or Both I and II. Hence 0,2,1,3 all are element of the set A. i.e. A = {0,1,2,3}. Also (3,2) ∈ A × A ⇒ Both statements are true.

questions.text: The sum of the first n terms of a series S is 3n² + 5n. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The terms of S form an arithmetic progression with common ratio 6.
The terms of S form a geometric progression having first term 8.
The terms of S form an arithmetic progression with common difference 14.
The terms of S form an arithmetic progression with common difference 6.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: (d) or The terms of S form an arithmetic progression with common difference 6. Tₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 3n² + 5n − [3(n − 1)² + 5(n − 1)] = 6n + 2 ∴ T₁ = 8, T₂ = 14, T₃ = 20, ….. Above is an A.P., having 1st term = 8 and common difference = 6

questions.text:
Consider the following in respect of the circle 4x² + 4y² − 4ax − 4ay + a² = 0
(P) The circle touches both the axes.
(Q) The diameter of the circle is 2a.
(R) The centre of the circle lies on the line x + y = a.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

Official answer key is internally inconsistent: it prints option letter (b) (printed as 'Only (P) and (Q)') but states 'Only (P) and (R)', which is option (c). correctOption omitted; editor to resolve.

officialAnswer.text: (b) or Only (P) and (R). ⇒ (x − a/2)² + (y − a/2)² = (a/2)² ∴ Centre (a/2, a/2), Radius: a/2 ⇒ The circle touches both the axes. Diameter = a. (a/2, a/2) satisfies x + y = a.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): Cardinal number of the power set of {{0, {1}, 3}}= 8
Reason (R): If A is a set with n(A) = m, the n (P(A)) = 2ᵐ
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true and Reason is false.
Assertion is false and Reason is true.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: (d) or A is false but R is true. Cardinal number of the set = 1 ⇒ Cardinal number of the power set of {{0, {1}, 3}} = 2¹ = 2. Hence Assertion (A): is false. Reason (R): If A is a set with n(A) = m, the n (P(A)) = 2ᵐ is true.

questions.text:
Coordinate of the point P is (2, 4, 5).
Assertion: The image of the point F in YZ plane is (−2,4,5).
Reason: When reflecting a point (x, y, z) in the XOY plane, the Z-coordinate changes its sign. The reflected point becomes (x, y, −z).
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true and Reason is false.
Assertion is false and Reason is true.

officialAnswer.text: (d) or A is false but R is true. ⇒ coordinate of the point F is (2, 0, 5). [∵ F lies on ZX plane] ∴ The image of the point F in YZ plane is (−2,0,5). Hence Assertion (A): is false. Reason is true.

Imagine you are designing a straight ramp that needs to connect two points at different elevations. Point P is at a horizontal distance of 10 meters and a vertical height of 2 meters from the starting point Q.
Write the equation of the line representing the ramp, considering the starting point Q as the origin. What is the angle of inclination of the ramp?
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: The ramp connects Q(0, 0) and P(10, 2). The equation of the ramp is y = x/5 or x − 5y = 0. tanθ = m = 1/5, θ = tan⁻¹(1/5) ≈ (11.31)°.

questions.text:
If a, b and c (a > 0, c > 0) are in G.P, justify the following with respect to the equation ax² + bx + c = 0:
(i) The equation has imaginary roots.
(ii) The product of the roots of the equation b²/a²
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: Given, a, b and c ⇒ b² = ac. (i) Discriminant (D) = b² − 4ac = ac − 4ac = −3ac < 0, since a, c > 0. Hence equation has imaginary roots. (ii) Product of the roots = c/a = ac/a² = b²/a²

questions.text: If f(x) = x sinx/(1 + cosx), then find f′(π/2).
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: f(x) = x sinx/(1+cosx) = x × 2 sin(x/2) cos(x/2)/(2cos²(x/2)) = x tan(x/2). f′(x) = tan(x/2) + (x/2) sec²(x/2) ∴ f′(π/2) = tan(π/4) + (π/4) sec²(π/4) = 1 + π/2

questions.text: If the sum of binomial coefficients in the expansion of (x + y)ⁿ is 256, then in which term of the expansion does the greatest binomial coefficient occurs?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: ⇒ 2ⁿ = 256 ⇒ 2ⁿ = 2⁸ ⇒ n = 8. ∴ Total number of terms = 8 + 1 = 9. The coefficient of middle most term is the greatest. Hence ((9+1)/2)th i.e. 5th term coefficient is the greatest.

questions.text: Does lim_(x→0) |sinx|/x exist? Give justification.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: L.H.L. = lt_(x→0⁻) |sinx|/x = lt_(x→0⁻) −(sinx)/x = −1. R.H.L. = lt_(x→0⁺) |sinx|/x = lt_(x→0⁺) sinx/x = 1. ∴ L.H.L. ≠ R.H.L. ∴ limit does not exist

questions.text: Evaluate: lt_(x→π) (1 − Sin(x/2)) / (Cos(x/2)[Cos(x/4) − Sin(x/4)])
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: = lt_(x→π) (Cos(x/4) − Sin(x/4))² / ((Cos²(x/4) − Sin²(x/4))(Cos(x/4) − Sin(x/4))) = lt_(x→π) 1/(Cos(x/4) + Sin(x/4)). By applying limit, we get = 1/(Cos(π/4) + Sin(π/4)) = 1/(1/√2 + 1/√2) = √2/2 = 1/√2 Ans.

questions.text: Two finite sets have 'm' and 'n' elements. The number of subsets of the first set is 112 more than that of second set. Find the values of 'm' and 'n'.
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: 2ᵐ − 2ⁿ = 112 ⇒ 2ⁿ(2ᵐ⁻ⁿ − 1) = 2⁴ × 7. On comparing we get n = 4 and 2ᵐ⁻ⁿ − 1 = 7 ⇒ 2ᵐ⁻ⁿ = 8 = 2³ ⇒ m − n = 3 ⇒ m = 7. Ans. m=7, n=4

extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: P(1st card a king) = 4/52 = 1/13. P(2nd card a king) = 3/51 = 1/17. ∴ Probability of Both Cards being Kings = 1/13 × 1/17 = 1/221

questions.text:
A (1,2,3), B (0,4,1), C(−1, −1, −3) are the vertices of a triangle ABC. Find the following:
(i) Length of AB and AC. [1]
(ii) Coordinates of the point in which the bisector of the ∠BAC meets BC. [2]
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.
Answer key heading prints [4] for Question 9; the question paper prints [3].

officialAnswer.text: (i) Length AB = 3 and AC = 7. (ii) By the Angle Bisector Theorem, D divides BC internally in the ratio AB : AC = 3 : 7. Applying section formula, the coordinates of the point where the bisector of ∠BAC meets BC are (−3/10, 5/2, −1/5).

questions.text: Given that α and β are the roots of qx² − px + r = 0, form an equation whose roots are α + 1/β and β + 1/α.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: α + β = p/q, α.β = r/q. S = α + β + (α+β)/(αβ) = p/q + p/r = p((q+r)/(qr)). P = αβ + 1/(αβ) + 2 = r/q + q/r + 2 = (q+r)²/(qr). Required equation: x² − p((q+r)/(qr))x + (q+r)²/(qr) = 0

questions.text: Find the points of intersection of the line y = x + 1 and the circle x² + y² = 5. Hence or otherwise, find the length of the chord.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: x² + (x + 1)² = 5 ⇒ x² + x − 2 = 0 ⇒ (x + 2)(x − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = −2 or x = 1. The line intersects the circle at the points (−2, −1) and (1,2). Length of the chord = √((1 + 2)² + (2 + 1)²) = √18 = 3√2 Units

questions.text: If 2 − i√3 where i = √−1 is a root of the equation x² + ax + b = 0, then find the value of a + b.

officialAnswer.text: Other root is 2 + i√3. S = 4, P = (2 − i√3)(2 + i√3) = 4 + 3 = 7. ⇒ x² − 4x + 7 = 0. On comparing we get, a = −4, b = 7. ∴ a + b = −4 + 7 = 3.

questions.text: If z is a complex number such that (z−1)/(z+1) is purely imaginary, then what is |z| equal to?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: Let z = x + iy. Since (z − 1)/(z + 1) is purely imaginary ⇒ Re((z−1)/(z+1)) = 0 ⇒ (x² − 1 + y²)/((x + 1)² + y²) = 0 ⇒ x² + y² = 1 ⇒ |z|² = 1 ⇒ |z| = 1

questions.text:
The curve G has equation y = 1 − x³ − 6x² − 9x and part of the graph of G is shown below:
(a) Find the derivative of y with respect to x.
(b) If the tangents drawn to the curve at the points B and C are parallel to x-axis, then find the coordinates of B and C respectively.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: (a) dy/dx = −3x² − 12x − 9. (b) dy/dx = 0 ⇒ x² + 4x + 3 = 0 ⇒ (x + 3)(x + 1) = 0 ⇒ x = −3, −1. When x = −3, y = 1; when x = −1, y = 5. Hence, coordinates of B(−3,1), C(−1,5).

questions.text:
If A and B are two acute angles having its sum equal to π/4, then answer the following:
(a) Find the value of (cotA − 1)(cotB − 1).
(b) Hence, find the value of cot(π/8).
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.

officialAnswer.text: (a) A + B = π/4 ⇒ cot(A + B) = 1 ⇒ (cot A.cot B − 1)/(cot B + cot A) = 1 ⇒ … ⇒ (cotA − 1)(cotB − 1) = 2. (b) ∵ π/8 + π/8 = π/4 ∴ (cot(π/8) − 1)² = 2 ∴ cot(π/8) − 1 = ±√2 ⇒ cot(π/8) = √2 + 1 (as π/8 = acute angle ∴ cot(π/8) = +ve) Ans.

questions.text: A focal chord of the parabola y² = 8x makes an angle of 60° with the x − axis. Find the length of this focal chord.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.
Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: 4a = 8, a = 2, focus S(2,0). Line: y = √3x − 2√3. Substituting: 3x² − 20x + 12 = 0; x₁ + x₂ = 20/3, x₁x₂ = 4; (x₂ − x₁)² = 400/9 − 16 = 256/9 ⇒ x₂ − x₁ = 16/3. Length of focal chord = 2(x₂ − x₁) = 2 × 16/3 = 32/3 units.

questions.text:
A satellite moves in an Elliptical orbit around the earth as shown in the figure below. It moves so that the sum of its distances from the points f2 (-2,0) and f1 (2,0) is 8 units.
Based on the above information, find the following:
(a) The length of its semi-major axis of the elliptical orbit. [1]
(b) Eccentricity of the elliptical orbit. [1]
(c) Equation of the elliptical orbit. [2]
(d) Distance between f1 and P(Perigee). [1]
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: 2a = 8. (a) Length of semi-major axis a is 4 units. ae = 2 (b) ⇒ e = 2/4 = 1/2. Using b² = a²(1 − e²), b² = 12. (c) Required equation of elliptical orbit is x²/16 + y²/12 = 1. (d) f₁P = a − ae = 4 − 2 = 2 units.

questions.text: For the word 'DEVASTATION', determine the number of 4-letter combinations and 4-letter permutations.
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.
Answer key's final permutation total (702) is reproduced as printed.

officialAnswer.text: Case I: 4 distinct letters from 9: C(9,4) = 126. Case II: one pair from [AA, TT] and 2 distinct from 8: C(2,1) × C(8,2) = 56. Case III: two pairs: C(2,2) = 1. ∴ Total number of selections = 126 + 56 + 1 = 183. Total number of permutations = 126 × 4! + 56 × 4!/2! + 1 × 4!/(2!×2!) = 126 × 24 + 56 × 12 + 1 × 6 = 702.

questions.text:
The letters of the word ‘CRICKET’ are written in all possible orders.
(a) Find the total number words with or without meaning. [1]
(b) If these words are written out as in a dictionary, find the rank of the word ‘CRICKET’. [4]
extractionIssues: Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Total number of words = 7!/2! = 2520. (b) CC***** = 120, CE***** = 120, CI***** = 120, CK***** = 120, CRC**** = 24, CRE**** = 24, CRICE** = 2; Total = 530. The next word is CRICKET. Hence the rank of the word CRICKET is 531.

questions.text:
Evaluate: cos α + cos(α + 2π/3) + cos(α + 4π/3). [2]
(a) Hence prove that: [1]
cos³α + cos³(α + 2π/3) + cos³(α + 4π/3) = 3 cos α cos(α + 2π/3) cos(α + 4π/3)
(b) If cos³α + cos³(α + 2π/3) + cos³(α + 4π/3) = (k/(k+1)) cos kα, find k. [2]
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers); check against the PDF. Checked against the rendered page.
Official answer notation (fractions/powers) rebuilt from the answer-key page render; working trimmed to value points.

officialAnswer.text: cos α + {cos(4π/3 + α) + cos(2π/3 + α)} = cos α + 2 cos(π + α) cos(π/3) = cos α − 2 cos α . 1/2 = 0. With x = cos α, y = cos(2π/3 + α), z = cos(4π/3 + α): if x + y + z = 0 then x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz, which proves (a). 3 cos α cos(α + 2π/3) cos(α + 4π/3) = … = (3/4) cos α {4cos²α − 3} = (3/4) cos 3α ∴ k = 3

Find the mean and standard deviation using the deviation method for the following:
Age | 20-25 | 25-30 | 30-35 | 35-40 | 40-45 | 45-50 | 50-55
No of employees | 170 | 110 | 80 | 45 | 40 | 30 | 25
Find the percentage of the employees in an organisation whose age lies between x̄ − σ and x̄ + σ.
